texts.preamble: P.Iyappan vs State Represented By on 22 October, 2019 Author: G.R.Swaminathan Bench: G.R.Swaminathan 1 Before The Madurai Bench Of Madras High Court Dated : 22.10.2019 Coram The Honourable Mr.Justice G.R.Swaminathan CRL.O.P.(MD)No.5276 of 2015 and M.P.(MD)Nos.1 and 2 of 2015 1. P.Iyappan 2. Panneerselvam 3. Mahendran Dominic 4. S.Saroja ... Petitioners/Accused Nos.1 to 4 Vs. State represented by, Food Safety Officer, Vickramasingapuram, Tirunelveli District. ... Respondent/Complainant Prayer : Criminal Original petition is filed under Section 482 of Cr.P.C., to admit this quash petition on file, to call for the records in C.C.No.262 of 2014 on the file of the Judicial Magistrate, Ambasamudram, Tirunelveli District and to quash the same. For Petitioners : Mr.V.Kathirvelu, Senior Counsel, for Mr.K.Prabhu. For Respondent : Mr.A.Robinson, Government Advocate(Crl. Side). *
texts.facts: On 21.04.2014, at about 2.00 p.m., the respondent herein went to the shop run by the second petitioner Panneerselvam in the name and style of V.Mani Store and purchased 48 samples of Sindhu Mutton Roast Masala. Each pack weighed 20 grams and was priced at Rs.5/-. At that time, the first petitioner Iyappan was in the shop premises as its salesman. When he enquired, the first petitioner replied that the said packets were purchased from the third petitioner who is the wholesaler. 3. It is not in dispute that the food item was manufactured by the fourth petitioner herein. All the packets http://www.judis.nic.in were fully sealed. The samples were sent for analysis. The report of the analyst revealed that the food item contained Sunset Yellow. The food analyst gave his opinion to the effect that the sample sent by the respondent is unsafe under Section 3(1)(zz) of the Food Safety and Standards Act 2006, since it contained added colouring matter, the addition of which is prohibited under Regulation 3.1.2(1) of Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulation 2011. It also contained 'Flavour Enhancement'. Based on the report of the Food Analyst, the respondent instituted the impugned private complaint before the Judicial Magistrate, Ambasamudram. Cognizance of the offences under Section 59(1) and 63 of the Food Safety and Standards Act was taken and summons were issued to the petitioners herein. To quash the same, this criminal original petition came to be filed. It is not in dispute that the first petitioner is the salesman and the second petitioner is the shop owner, while the third petitioner is the wholesaler.
texts.arguments: 4. Section 27 of the Food Safety and Standards Act 2006 reads as under:- http://www.judis.nic.in 27.Liability of Manufacturers, packers, wholesalers, distributors and sellers (1) The manufacturer or packer of an article of food shall be liable for such article of food if it does not meet the requirements of this Act and the rules and regulations made thereunder. (2) The wholesaler or distributor shall be liable under this Act for any article of food which is - (a) supplied after the date of its expiry; or (b) stored or supplied in violation of the safety instructions of the manufacturer; or (c) unsafe or misbranded, or (d) unidentifiable of manufacturer from whom the article of food have been received; or P.Iyappan vs State Represented By on 22 October, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58240584/ 2 (e) stored or handled or kept in violation of the provisions of this Act, the http://www.judis.nic.in rules and regulations made thereunder; or (f)received by him with knowledge of being unsafe. (3) The seller shall be liable under this Act, for any article of food which is - (a)sold after the date of its expiry; or (b)handled or kept in unhygienic conditions; or (c) misbranded; or (d)unidentifiable of the manufacturer or the distributors from whom such articles of food were received; or (e)received by him with knowledge of being unsafe. 5.
